title: Building the Context Engine AI Agents Need
summary: Unblocked DevRel pitch for an organizational context engine; argues rules files, MCPs and big windows are insufficient.

assertions.quote: nearly 50% less tokens used ... With context, it actually one-shot the prompt

verdicts.note: Relevant org context plausibly cuts rework, but the cited 50% token / one-shot result is a single vendor test, not independent evidence.

assertions.quote: static content in a repo, which is going to rot like every other documentation you ever wrote

verdicts.note: Agents treat repo docs as authoritative; outdated docs demonstrably steer them wrong.

assertions.quote: people think that more rules and Claude MD files will fix this ... Claude was like just completely ignored it

verdicts.note: Persistent instruction files measurably steer agent behavior; overlong or contradictory ones reduce adherence.

assertions.quote: agents don't know actually when to call them ... it becomes a bit of a mess

verdicts.note: Tool-selection accuracy drops as tool count grows (e.g. Berkeley function-calling and RAG-MCP results); dynamic tool loadouts help.

assertions.quote: if you go over 40% of the context window, you enter the dumb zone

verdicts.note: Long-context benchmarks (e.g. NoLiMa, context-rot studies) show degradation as context grows; the exact threshold is model-dependent.

assertions.quote: you then kind of force a problem which is a bottleneck at code review

verdicts.note: Surveys and studies (e.g. Faros, Google) report increased PR volume and review load with AI adoption.
The review finds developer work shifts from writing code toward specification, supervision and validation, with the unit of work moving to the acceptance decision.
